clue.text: By going back to fish, gets censure

indicators.note: going back tells us the word for 'by' is read from right to left

parts.note: per is Latin for 'by', as in 'per annum'
the roach is a common freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone who abandons a plan by returning to fishing earns criticism for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns the Latin word upside down to make REP; 'gets' is a link, and the fish is not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to rebuke or blame them, the same as censuring them.

clue.text: Embarrassed girl in Cornish town

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red
Ruth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A blushing young woman in a town in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Redruth is a former mining town in Cornwall, the county at England's south-western tip.

clue.text: Literary work of two kinds

parts.note: read as a piece of writing that belongs to two literary forms at once, the ordinary and the verse

explanation.surface: A book combining two genres.
explanation.definitionFit: A prose poem is a composition written in prose but with the qualities of verse.

clue.text: Keep note, say?

explanation.surface: Asking whether to retain a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks 'note' as just one example of the sense of remarking.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe a rule or festival is to keep it, and to observe can mean to notice or to remark.

clue.text: Grateful for making the path

parts.note: read 'Grateful' as a fireplace grate full of ash, the residue spread to make a garden or running track

explanation.surface: Thanks to the person who laid the footpath.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt coal residue from a grate was used to surface paths and running tracks.

clue.text: Priest has replaced prophet

parts.note: Eli is the priest of Shiloh in the Old Testament who brought up Samuel

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of 'has' are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A clergyman has been superseded by a seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges the letters of 'has' to make SHA; the surface reads 'replaced' as a verb about the priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Elisha was the Old Testament seer who succeeded Elijah.

clue.text: German city overcomes rise in French milk — a " must *"

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word placed over another comes before it

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr in Germany

indicators.note: rise in a down clue tells us the French word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lait is the French word for milk

explanation.surface: A German city triumphs over a rising price of milk in France, which is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise in' turns the French word to make TIAL; in a down clue 'overcomes' puts the German city on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is indispensable, something one has to have.

clue.text: Pim is broke — learning to beg.

indicators.note: broke here means broken up, so the letters of 'Pim' are reordered

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge

explanation.surface: A penniless man named Pim takes up study to plead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is broke' rearranges PIM into IMP, followed by LORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to plead or entreat earnestly.

clue.text: Blunders into monkeys ?

explanation.surface: Clumsy errors made by a troop of apes.
explanation.definitionFit: A glaring mistake is a howler, and howlers are loud-voiced tropical American monkeys.

clue.text: Words mis-spelt in letter written-prelude to retirement

indicators.note: mis-spelt says the letters of 'Words' are set down in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
the letter S written out in full is spelt ESS

explanation.surface: Someone misspells words in a letter just before retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mis-spelt' rearranges WORDS into DROWS; then IN, then ESS, the name of the letter S. 'Retirement' here means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepiness is what comes before going to bed, and retiring is a polite word for going to bed.

clue.text: Pledge a future queen ?

explanation.surface: A promise made to the woman who will one day reign.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess a pawn that reaches the far side of the board is promoted, usually to a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left with a broker as security is a pledge, and the lowly chess piece may later be promoted to a queen.

clue.text: Means we have got out of the capital

definitions.text: Means we have got out of the capital

parts.words: Means we have got out of the capital
parts.note: read as money we draw from invested funds rather than from work, not as a way of escaping a city

explanation.surface: A way we found of escaping from the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Money from investments rather than wages is income not worked for, drawn from one's capital.

clue.text: Boats for anglers ?

parts.note: read as craft that fish with lines, the crew being people who catch fish on lines

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of boats fishermen use.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooker is a type of small fishing boat, especially in Ireland, and anglers catch fish on hooks.

clue.text: Physical feature carried -by invader in 55 BC

definitions.text: Physical feature carried -by invader in 55 BC

parts.words: Physical feature carried -by invader in 55 BC
parts.note: read as the facial shape associated with Julius Caesar, who landed in Britain in 55 BC

explanation.surface: A bodily characteristic of the man who came to Britain in 55 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooked or aquiline profile with a high bridge is named after the people of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Something to be cured by a seaside trip

indicators.note: trip suggests stumbling, so the letters of 'seaside' fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An illness that a day at the beach will put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges SEASIDE; the surface pretends a seaside outing is the cure.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or ailment is what a doctor tries to cure.

clue.text: Doing away with a lob put up — one gets in to smash

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: smash means break into pieces, so the letters of 'in to' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ending a lofted shot in tennis by putting it away with a smash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns LOB into BOL, and 'smash' rearranges IN TO into TION. The tennis surface hides that 'in to' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Abolition is the act of ending or annulling something such as a law or practice.

clue.text: Little boy, with traffic hold-ups, gets the fidgets

parts.note: Jim is a short form of the boy's name James
traffic jams are hold-ups on the road

explanation.surface: A small child stuck in traffic queues becomes restless.
explanation.definitionFit: The jim-jams is an informal phrase for nervous restlessness or jitters.

clue.text: Shows sloth at home-irate when corrected

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: corrected means put right, so the letters of 'irate' are reordered

explanation.surface: Laziness at home makes someone angry when told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when corrected' rearranges IRATE into ERTIA; 'Shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia means sluggishness or reluctance to act, like laziness.

clue.text: Garments seen in spring ?

parts.note: read 'spring' as leap rather than the season: people who leap, as well as knitted tops

explanation.surface: Clothes worn in the springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen pullover is so called in Britain, and those who leap are the same word.

clue.text: Singer, about fifty, takes £500, in total

indicators.note: about says the singer goes around the Roman numeral for fifty

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
the pound sign is L, from libra, and D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A middle-aged vocalist earns a fee of five hundred pounds altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped the pound sign. 'about' puts L inside ALTO to give ALLTO; then L for pound and D for 500.
explanation.definitionFit: All told is an idiom meaning when everything is counted, altogether.

clue.text: Look to a bit of golf for a breathing-space

parts.note: air means appearance or look, as in 'an air of mystery'
a golf course is divided into holes

explanation.surface: Turning to a round of golf for some rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent that lets air through is a literal breathing space.

clue.text: Fish carries the can, possibly, in school

indicators.note: carries means the fish holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of 'can' may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A fish takes the blame at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges 'can' into ANC. Lancing College is an English public school in Sussex; 'carries the can' means takes the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancing is a well-known boarding institution in West Sussex.

clue.text: Chaperons of the foreign type on Anne's trip

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'

indicators.note: trip suggests a stumble, so the letters of 'Anne's' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Foreign escorts accompany Anne on her journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges the letters of 'Anne's' into ENNAS; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who acts as chaperone to girls, especially in Spain.

clue.text: Lear character takes club and dies sadly for the king

parts.note: Edmund is the scheming bastard son of Gloucester in King Lear
an iron is a kind of golf club

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of 'dies' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A character in Shakespeare's tragedy seizes a weapon and dies in grief over the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' turns DIES into SIDE. Edmund II, called Ironside, was an English king in 1016.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Ironside was an Anglo-Saxon monarch of England, briefly reigning in 1016.

clue.text: Some nasty excrescence on the lid ?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of an unpleasant growth sits on the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the edge of an eyelid is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: House party see work-place

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a position is a place or location

explanation.surface: Members of a political party visit a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link here. The House is the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: In the House of Commons the main party not in government is formally called Her Majesty's Opposition.

clue.text: Standard view of: man of religion

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
to see something is to view it

explanation.surface: A clergyman's usual outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parsi is a follower of Zoroastrianism in India, descended from Persian refugees.

clue.text: Chemicals supplied by Sergeant Turner

indicators.note: a turner is something that turns, so it rearranges the letters of 'Sergeant'

explanation.surface: A painter called Turner who was an army sergeant supplied some chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the name of the sergeant or the painter, but it signals that SERGEANT is turned into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Reagents are substances used in chemical reactions to detect or produce other substances.
